question: How does the amended Reg S-P impact broker-dealers, and where does it overlap with rules they may already follow?

program.title: Reg S-P obligations for broker-dealers, mapped against neighboring rules
program.thesis: Deconstruct Reg S-P §248.30 and four neighboring security and breach rules into individual obligations; classify each by type, whether it binds a broker-dealer, and how fast it must be done; then pair every Reg S-P obligation with comparable obligations elsewhere to separate genuinely new work from work a firm may already do.

unit.rationale: Every paragraph of Reg S-P §248.30 and four neighboring security and breach rules; the first layer gates to actual obligations (list items like '(iii) Notify each affected individual' carry duties even when they read as fragments).

doc_notes.note: Reg S-P §248.30 applies to 'covered institutions': SEC-registered broker-dealers (including funding portals), investment companies, registered investment advisers, and registered transfer agents. The 2024 amendments added the incident response program, customer notification (as soon as practicable, no later than 30 days), and service provider oversight requirements.

The FTC Safeguards Rule applies to financial institutions under FTC jurisdiction (e.g. non-bank lenders, mortgage brokers, payment firms). SEC-registered broker-dealers are regulated by the SEC under Regulation S-P instead and are not subject to this rule.

The HIPAA Security Rule applies to HIPAA covered entities (health plans, health care clearinghouses, and health care providers that transmit health information electronically) and their business associates. It does not apply to broker-dealers acting as such.

The HIPAA Breach Notification Rule applies to HIPAA covered entities and their business associates, for breaches of unsecured protected health information. It does not apply to broker-dealers acting as such.

SEC Regulation S-K Item 106 applies to public companies (SEC registrants filing annual reports). It binds a broker-dealer only if the broker-dealer or its parent is a public registrant; it is a disclosure requirement, not an operational one.

nodes.label: Obligation?
nodes.question: Does this text impose a concrete duty on a regulated organization (something it must do or must not do), rather than only defining terms, describing scope, or cross-referencing?

options.description: Adopt or maintain written policies, procedures, or a security program
Assess risks, test, audit, or monitor safeguards
Implement specific technical, physical, or administrative controls
Detect, contain, assess, or investigate a security incident
Notify affected individuals, regulators, or others about an incident or breach
Select, contract with, or oversee service providers or third parties
Keep records, document actions, or dispose of information
Board or management oversight, reporting, or public disclosure

relations.label: Overlap between Reg S-P and neighboring rules
